notes: Qwen models with reasoning (QwQ, Qwen3) use 'reasoning_content' field in the API response. They may also include <thinking>...</thinking> tags inline in the content text. Qwen3 served without a reasoning parser (llama.cpp, vLLM without --reasoning-parser) emits the plain think pair instead. All of these are handled by the reasoning adapter (see the reasoning-tag constants).

examples.name: reasoning_content with thinking tags

message.content:
<thinking>The user wants weather for Tokyo. I'll use my get_weather function.</thinking>
{"tool": "get_weather", "args": {"location": "Tokyo"}}
message.reasoning_content:
The user wants weather for Tokyo. I'll use my get_weather function.

{"tool": "get_weather", "args": {"location": "Tokyo"}}

examples.expected_extracted_reasoning:
The user wants weather for Tokyo. I'll use my get_weather function.

{"tool": "get_weather", "args": {"location": "Tokyo"}}

examples.name: text response with thinking tags

message.content:
<thinking>Simple greeting, no tool needed.</thinking>
Hello! How can I help you today?

examples.expected_clean_content: Hello! How can I help you today?

examples.name: no reasoning field

message.content: Hello! How can I help you today?

examples.expected_clean_content: Hello! How can I help you today?

examples.name: plain think tags in content

message.content:
<think>
The user wants weather for Tokyo. I'll call get_weather.
</think>

{"tool": "get_weather", "args": {"location": "Tokyo"}}

examples.expected_extracted_reasoning: The user wants weather for Tokyo. I'll call get_weather.
